summary: No NEW Medium+ findings. All four hunt targets empirically refuted as correct/benign-by-design on a live mainnet fork. Minter authority transitions never leave phUSD with zero authorized minters (old minter overlaps new through steps 1-2, revoked only in step 3 after new minter is live; the staker reward path is a SEPARATE independent phUSD minter and is never touched). The 4000/day cap governs ONLY user-facing collateral mint() and cannot brick the migration (Phase-4 prefund uses owner-gated withdrawAsOwner, not minting) nor staker rewards (staker mints phUSD directly, uncapped). Evacuate/reseed reads principalOf fresh so it cannot double-count; the round-trip haircut (~2.097 DOLA on a 13816 DOLA position, ~0.015%) is the intended minter shock-absorber. 6fd3eddc/YS PhusdMinterRepoint superseded is CONFIRMED correct: the fresh deploy is the same PhusdStableMinter source whose public ABI is a strict superset of the old build, and there are NO on-chain contract callers (mint() is user-facing only; SYA/Phlimbo do not call the minter), so no ABI drift (YS-20 pattern) is introduced. ys-swap-deployments.json field set written by step 1 covers every downstream read; step 2/5 use key-path merge that preserves step 1 fields.

empiricalVerifications.evidence: old minter canMint stays true through step1 (temp staker added) and step2 (new minter added, two coexist); revoked only in step3. Staker (0xbce8) authorizedMinters never modified by any of the 4 scripts.

empiricalVerifications.claim: Phase-4 prefund (step5) survives step3 client revocation
empiricalVerifications.evidence: after step3 deauthorizes OLD_MINTER as client on YS_DOLA_OLD, owner-gated withdrawAsOwner still drains it: booked 13816.564 DOLA, recovered 13815.459 DOLA. Mapper's 'Phase-4 survives revocation by design' VERIFIED TRUE; step5 does not brick.

empiricalVerifications.claim: 4000/day cap blocks only user mint, not staker rewards / migration
empiricalVerifications.evidence: newMinter.mint(DOLA,5000e18) reverts 'Daily mint limit exceeded'; mint(DOLA,4000e18) succeeds; ORIG staker mints 100000e18 phUSD directly with no cap (staker is its own authorized minter). Migration prefund path (withdrawAsOwner) mints nothing.

empiricalVerifications.claim: Evacuate/reseed (step10) moves residual to V2 under new minter, no double-count
empiricalVerifications.evidence: reads principalOf(OLD_MINTER) fresh (13816.564 DOLA), withdraws, reseeds 13814.467 DOLA onto ysDolaV2 under newMinter; old minter principal zeroed (post-assert). Round-trip shortfall 2.097 DOLA (~0.015%) = redeem+deposit haircut, intended minter absorption.

empiricalVerifications.method: cast getYieldStrategies on both SYAs + progress.replace-sya.1.json

Step 1's SYA=0x3C69 is the live one. (Step 11's SYA=0x3bBE targets the decommissioned SYA - that is a STEP-11 cluster bug, out of this sub-saga's assignment; see clusterNote.)

lowFindings.title: phoenix-ui mainnet-addresses.ts repoint is a manual out-of-worktree step; if skipped, UI users hit revert on the revoked old minter until updated
lowFindings.description: Step 3 revokes the old minter's phUSD mint authority on-chain and the post-step JS patches only the IN-REPO server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts. The phoenix-ui repo's own mainnet-addresses.ts lives outside this worktree (Q-REFS) and must be hand-edited + redeployed. Until then the UI keeps users pointed at OLD_MINTER, whose mint() now reverts 'phUSD.mint: not authorized'.
lowFindings.impact: Temporary user-facing mint outage (no fund loss, fails loud). Recoverable by updating the UI.
lowFindings.evidence: CutoverAndRevokeOldMinter.s.sol:142-143 + patch script Q-REFS note; mainnet-addresses.ts:31 still OLD_MINTER pre-patch.
lowFindings.recommendation: Add a release-checklist gate (or CI) coupling the on-chain revocation to the phoenix-ui repoint+redeploy so they ship atomically; or stage the UI repoint BEFORE the revoke broadcast.

lowFindings.title: Step 1 has no 'already deployed' checkpoint; a mid-saga re-run silently redeploys V2/temp/migrators and overwrites the deployments bus
lowFindings.description: The five `new` deployments in step 1 are unconditional (only the WIRING is idempotent). Re-running step 1 after steps 2-3 already broadcast against the first deployment produces a NEW V2/tempStaker/migrator set and overwrites ys-swap-deployments.json, while the live phUSD-minter wiring + old-strategy revocation still reference the FIRST set. Downstream preflights (code.length, canMint, config-match) catch most mismatches and revert, so this is largely fail-loud, but the bus now points at un-wired contracts.
lowFindings.impact: Operator footgun on re-run; downstream steps revert (no silent corruption thanks to guards). Stale bus must be manually restored.
lowFindings.recommendation: Gate deployment on a 'deployments JSON already present with live-code addresses' check, or document that step 1 is run exactly once and never re-run after step 2.

clusterNote.detail: INCONSISTENCY-SYA resolved empirically: step 1 (mine) correctly registers V2 on the LIVE SYA 0x3C69. Step 11 DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA (NOT in this assignment) targets the DECOMMISSIONED, EMPTY SYA 0x3bBE - its removeYieldStrategy calls no-op (idempotent skip on _isRegistered) and the OLD strategies remain registered on the live 0x3C69 forever. This is a step-11 correctness/intent-mismatch bug (likely Medium: deregistration is a no-op, old strategies never removed from the live SYA strategy list) - flagged here for the agent auditing step 11/12 (DEREGISTER+DECOMMISSION sub-saga), not double-reported by this sub-saga.
clusterNote.recommendation: Verify step 11's LIVE_SYA constant against mainnet-addresses.ts at execution; it must be 0x3C69, not 0x3bBE.
